Does the selected change persist at broader scales?

Bray–Curtis at broader ranks can decrease when opposing member changes cancel. Family grouping uses taxonomic labels, not branch lengths. Weighted UniFrac uses the actual reference phylogeny; its numerical scale differs from Bray–Curtis, so a lower value does not mean a proportionally smaller biological or clinical effect.

Phylogeny coverage, method & functional-data status

Normalized weighted UniFrac = sum of branch length × absolute difference in descendant shares, divided by sum of branch length × summed descendant shares. Root stem excluded; no tip imputation, pseudocounts or re-rooting. Matching is by SGB identifier, including unresolved taxa.

How spread out are the reference groups themselves?

For each reference profile, calculate its median distance to all other profiles in its own group (self excluded). The table summarizes those per-profile medians. Which microbes contribute to the differences?

Rank microbes by their contribution to mean Bray–Curtis abundance distance from the selected reference group, averaged equally across Sid’s five visits. This explains abundance differences; it is a separate calculation from the weighted UniFrac similarity plot above.

Visit cells show Sid minus the reference median in percentage points (pp). Red = higher; teal = lower. Colors do not imply benefit or harm. Click a taxon for its trajectory.

Red points: Sid. Shaded band: the reference group’s 10th–90th percentile abundance; dashed line: its median. This cross-sectional reference distribution is repeated across the timeline, not a longitudinal reference trajectory. Percentages use the retained, renormalized SGB profiles; they may differ slightly from the original within-Sid panels.

Contribution method, consistency & limitations

For a taxon and Sid visit, its contribution is ½ × the mean absolute difference in normalized share from every reference profile. Contributions sum exactly to the mean pairwise Bray–Curtis distance at the selected taxonomic rank. “Share of distance” divides the taxon’s five-visit mean contribution by the total five-visit mean distance, including hidden or unresolved features. Genus aggregation can cancel opposing SGB differences; it is not the SGB-distance decomposition. No contribution to weighted UniFrac is claimed.

Direction is measured relative to the reference median at each visit. A large contribution can coexist with little median difference if the reference cohort is highly variable. “Beyond middle 80% at all 5” requires every visit to be above the reference 90th percentile, or every visit below its 10th percentile. These are descriptive filters, not statistical significance. Zeros mean not detected in the supplied profiles. The five visits are repeated observations from one person.

The exact same retained SGB profiles, exclusions and coverage threshold used in the ordination are used here. Named shared genera agree between sources. For unresolved shared SGBs, UFPF’s GGB labels provide consistent grouping; unresolved Sid-only bins remain separate. Placeholder labels are not identified species. Group differences may reflect study procedures, medication, bowel preparation, diet and individual variation. Sid’s underlying weight units and full processing equivalence remain unverified; no disease classifier, treatment effect or health score is calculated.

Full-distance comparison & nearest reference profiles

These summaries use the original distance matrix, not distances measured on the two-dimensional plot. Pairwise values are dependent; they are descriptive, not independent observations for a statistical test. A nearest profile’s diagnosis does not classify Sid.

Coverage, compatibility & reproducible methods

Features are the union of observed, unambiguously mapped SGB tips across both sources—not just microbes detected in both. Grouped SGB rows and the corresponding numeric identifiers in either cohort are excluded, along with non-SGB leaves and unmapped tips. Each retained profile is normalized to sum to one. No pseudocounts or rarefaction. Abundance filters elsewhere on this page do not change this comparison.

Weighted UniFrac uses the official mpa_vJun23_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202307 tree and normalized branch-weighted differences. The supplied root is retained and its stem excluded. Bray–Curtis is one half of the sum of absolute differences in those same retained shares. PCoA is recomputed for each reference subset. Negative eigenvalues are handled with a Lingoes correction; displayed percentages refer to the corrected positive inertia. Original distances are used for nearest profiles and downloadable matrices.

UFPF has 53 unambiguous Parkinson’s disease labels, 26 IBD labels, 16 controls and 1 conflicting diagnosis. UF-PF-2022-074-1N is labeled “Uncertain diagnosis” because the source says both Control and PD. It stays in the full and non-IBD views, but not diagnosis-specific views. IBD participants were in remission and sampled after beginning polyethylene-glycol bowel preparation. Most controls were spouses of participants with Parkinson’s disease; this is not a population-wide healthy reference. Sample ID prefixes are not used to infer repeated participants.

The exact database matches; Sid’s report states MetaPhlAn 4.1.1, while UFPF’s exact patch version is not verified. Sid’s supplied integer weight units and full preprocessing remain unverified. UFPF’s derived “counts” sheet is not used. Its relative-abundance sheet is the source here. Retained-mass screening checks sensitivity to exclusions; it cannot correct cross-study laboratory effects.

TRACEABLE BY DESIGN

Methods & provenance

Scope

Five stool profiles from the public summary, one person. Later archive collections are not imported in this version. Stool is not pooled with saliva, iHMP, or tumor specimens. The interval selector always compares an earlier visit with a later visit.

Abundance and deltas

Each supplied SGB abundance weight is divided by the total of all reported SGB weights in that visit. Genus and family views sum these shares; unresolved labels remain separate. Δ pp = 100 × (end share − start share). Fold = end / start only when the starting value is positive. No pseudocounts are added. Blank/absent source rows are encoded as zero (“not detected in the supplied profile”). No raw-read or absolute-cell interpretation is made.

Normalizing the downloaded weights reproduces all five Shannon and inverse-Simpson values in the lab report to two decimals. The first profile also matches the original lab CSV. This verifies arithmetic consistency, not the biological meaning of the source units or cross-visit batch equivalence. No inferential testing or technical error bars are justified by these single profiles.

Eligibility & clinical context

Default eligibility is at least 0.1% share in at least two of all five visits, with no minimum delta. These exploratory defaults are not statistical significance or a validated detection limit. Filtering is applied after the selected taxonomic aggregation and never renormalizes values. Export contains visible rows and filter settings. Clinical events are matched by inclusive date overlap with the selected window, plus optional padding, using a downloaded public events-table snapshot. Source ranges are retained; missing end dates are treated as dated entries, not ongoing therapy. No medication effect is inferred.

Longitudinal comparisons

Adjacent-visit community dissimilarity uses all features at the selected taxonomic level: ½ × sum of absolute differences in normalized shares (Bray–Curtis for these unit-sum profiles). It is not a rate, significance test, or estimate of a treatment effect. Persistence requires a positive abundance at or above the chosen floor in all five visits. Consistency ranks named features by (maximum − minimum) / median; unresolved features are excluded from this ranking. Genus and family aggregation can hide member turnover. The member table exposes opposing changes. Family-level features do not inherit species- or genus-specific evidence cards. Distance from the first visit is a descriptive comparison to an already-treated sample. Weighted UniFrac uses the exact vJun23_202307 reference tree and all 236 mapped SGBs; see the community trajectory provenance for formula and source hashes.

Treatment overlays share the microbiome date axis. Identical title/date/end-date/dose treatment entries are deduplicated across clinical timelines; source periods are clipped to the plot but retained in hover text. Exposure literature uses treatments overlapping the selected interval, independently of the overlay category and nearby-event padding. Cards are curated; exact-drug evidence is distinguished from broader class or response-association evidence. References were reviewed Oct 17, 2026. Date uncertainty and overlapping exposures prevent causal attribution.

Dates

Pipeline

MetaPhlAn 4.1.1 · mpa_vJun23_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202307, documented in the June 23, 2026 lab report covering the first six visits. Full preprocessing, extraction, and sample-level quality metrics have not been verified. UFPF uses the same reference database and is available as an exploratory comparison on this page; full processing equivalence remains unverified.

Taxonomy & literature

SGBs are species-level genome bins, not confirmed strains. LKT and other unresolved labels are not named genera or species; they do not receive name-matched evidence. Genus matches are explicitly broader than species matches. Akkermansia sp KLE1798 is not assumed to be A. muciniphila. Cards summarize selected primary studies, including limitations and conflicting cohort results; they are not a systematic review. Retrieval date: October 17, 2026.
